title: cuSZ-i: High-Ratio Scientific Lossy Compression on GPUs with Optimized Multi-Level Interpolation
problem: Existing GPU-based lossy compressors achieve low compression ratios and poor reconstruction quality, severely limiting their applicability to HPC scientific data reduction. High-ratio, high-quality error-bounded compression is needed to manage massive scientific datasets in modern HPC systems.
motivation: GPU-based compressors deliver substantially higher throughputs than CPU alternatives for scientific data compression, making them essential for HPC applications that need to efficiently reduce massive data volumes.
method: CUSZ-i predicts data values using multiple layers of interpolation on the GPU—estimating values between known data points at progressively finer scales—to reduce redundancy. It then applies Huffman encoding (replacing frequent patterns with shorter codes) and NVIDIA Bitcomp lossless compression to further shrink the data. The whole process guarantees decompressed data won't deviate more than your specified error threshold.
key_novelty: The core mechanism is using multiple layers of interpolation-based prediction on the GPU (estimating values between known data points at different scales) for data compression.
contributions: GPU-optimized interpolation-based prediction method for improved compression ratio and data quality
Optimized Huffman encoding module for enhanced efficiency
First integration of NVIDIA Bitcomp lossless compression as a compression-ratio-enhancing module
Demonstrates 476% compression ratio advantage over the second-best GPU-based lossy compressor

metrics.accuracy: compression ratio and error-bounded reconstruction quality
